name: Relay
author: E. T. Carter
description: A loom of fibre-optic strands carrying light. Thin dim fibres run the height of the frame and bright pulses race along them like data down glass, each a sharp head trailing a glowing comet tail. Every strand runs at its own speed and direction so the traffic is asynchronous — some pulses climbing, some falling — the strands lit in palette hues. Where carrier carried a waveform in the shape of the line, relay carries light travelling along a straight thread.

params.label: Strand spacing
params.effect: Distance between strands in CSS px; a dense ribbon cable at the minimum, a few wide channels at the maximum.

params.label: Strand width
params.effect: Half-width of each strand and its pulse in CSS px; fine glass fibre to thick glowing conduit.

params.label: Pulse speed
params.effect: How fast the pulses race along the strands; 0 holds them still, high streams the traffic briskly.

params.label: Traffic
params.effect: How many pulses ride each strand at once; low sends the occasional packet, high floods the fibres with a stream of light.

params.label: Tail length
params.effect: Length of each comet tail; short is a crisp travelling dot, long smears it into a glowing streak.

params.label: Glow
params.effect: Overall emission; low is a quiet cable, high a luminous data flood.

params.label: Resting fibre
params.effect: Brightness of the resting strand between pulses; 0 hides the fibres so only pulses show, high keeps every strand visibly lit.
